skill.name: ena-database
skill.description: Access European Nucleotide Archive APIs and bulk download references for public nucleotide sequences, reads, assemblies, taxonomy records, and metadata.
skill.summary: Retrieve public ENA sequence records, metadata, taxonomy details, and download guidance for bioinformatics workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The review found no prompt injection, credential access, filesystem writes, or covert exfiltration intent in the scanned files. Most static findings are false positives from public ENA API documentation and markdown fences; the only confirmed concern is the recommendation to use ftp:// for bulk public downloads.

remediation.issue: FTP download examples use an unencrypted transport for public sequence files.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer HTTPS or Aspera when available, and require checksum verification for every downloaded file.

remediation.issue: External network scope should be clear to users.
remediation.suggestion: Document that queries are sent to public ebi.ac.uk services, and avoid sending private sample metadata without user approval.

content.value_statement: Genomics teams need reliable access to ENA records without memorizing every endpoint. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through searches, downloads, and taxonomy lookups.
actual_capabilities: Explains ENA data types, including studies, samples, runs, assemblies, sequences, analyses, and taxonomy records.
Builds Portal API searches for samples, studies, reads, assemblies, sequences, analyses, and taxon records.
Retrieves record metadata through Browser API formats such as XML, text, FASTA, JSON, TSV, and CSV.
Guides FASTQ and assembly download planning through API file reports, FTP, Aspera, and enaBrowserTools.
Uses ENA taxonomy, cross-reference, and CRAM reference endpoints for common bioinformatics workflows.
limitations: It does not authenticate to private ENA services or manage restricted datasets.
It depends on live EBI services, network access, and current ENA API behavior.
Large file downloads may require external tools and local storage planning.
It does not validate biological conclusions from retrieved sequences or metadata.

use_cases.title: Find study samples
use_cases.description: A wet-lab researcher lists samples and metadata for a known study accession before analysis.

use_cases.title: Prepare raw read downloads
use_cases.description: A bioinformatics engineer retrieves FASTQ links, file sizes, and checksums for pipeline ingestion.

use_cases.title: Resolve taxonomy and references
use_cases.description: A data curator checks organism lineage, cross-references, and CRAM reference records for archive curation.

prompt_templates.title: Look up an accession
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner retrieval of one known ENA record.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the ENA record for accession ERR123456. Summarize its record type, linked study, sample, and available download formats.

prompt_templates.title: Search study experiments
prompt_templates.prompt: Search ENA for human RNA-Seq experiments from study PRJNA123456. Return accession IDs, sample titles, collection dates, and useful filters.

prompt_templates.title: Plan read downloads
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced file retrieval planning for pipeline input.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a plan to download FASTQ files for runs in study PRJEB1234. Include file links, sizes, checksums, rate limits, and retry guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Design a retrieval workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reproducible ENA data retrieval workflow for E. coli assemblies. Include Portal API queries, taxonomy checks, output formats, caching, and citation notes.

output_examples.output: A table-ready summary of sample accessions, titles, scientific names, collection dates, and notes about missing fields.
A download plan with FASTQ locations, file sizes, checksum fields, and a reminder to verify integrity after transfer.
A lineage summary for Escherichia coli, plus related taxonomy fields to include in downstream metadata.

best_practices: Verify accession IDs before running bulk downloads.
Use rate limiting, retry logic, and caching for repeated ENA queries.
Check MD5 values after downloading FASTQ, BAM, CRAM, or assembly files.
anti_patterns: Do not send private sample metadata unless the user approves external ENA requests.
Do not loop through large accession lists without delays or pagination.
Do not treat retrieved metadata as a biological interpretation without expert review.

faq.question: Does this skill require network access?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed to query public ENA and EBI endpoints.

faq.question: Can it download FASTQ files?
faq.answer: It can help find FASTQ links and plan downloads. Large transfers may need FTP, Aspera, or enaBrowserTools.

faq.question: Does it handle private data?
faq.answer: No. The skill targets public ENA records and does not manage authentication.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does it run bioinformatics analysis?
faq.answer: No. It retrieves and organizes ENA data for downstream analysis.

faq.question: How should I cite retrieved data?
faq.answer: Use study or project accessions, and include sample, run, or assembly accessions when relevant.
